From 5c47251e8c4903111608ddcba2a77c0c425c247c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Herve Codina <herve.codina@bootlin.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2023 16:26:55 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] lib/vsprintf: Fix %pfwf when current node refcount == 0

A refcount issue can appeared in __fwnode_link_del() due to the
pr_debug() call:
  WARNING: CPU: 0 PID: 901 at lib/refcount.c:25 refcount_warn_saturate+0xe5/0x110
  Call Trace:
  <TASK>
  ...
  of_node_get+0x1e/0x30
  of_fwnode_get+0x28/0x40
  fwnode_full_name_string+0x34/0x90
  fwnode_string+0xdb/0x140
  ...
  vsnprintf+0x17b/0x630
  ...
  __fwnode_link_del+0x25/0xa0
  fwnode_links_purge+0x39/0xb0
  of_node_release+0xd9/0x180
  ...

Indeed, an fwnode (of_node) is being destroyed and so, of_node_release()
is called because the of_node refcount reached 0.
From of_node_release() several function calls are done and lead to
a pr_debug() calls with %pfwf to print the fwnode full name.
The issue is not present if we change %pfwf to %pfwP.

To print the full name, %pfwf iterates over the current node and its
parents and obtain/drop a reference to all nodes involved.

In order to allow to print the full name (%pfwf) of a node while it is
being destroyed, do not obtain/drop a reference to this current node.

Fixes: a92eb7621b9f ("lib/vsprintf: Make use of fwnode API to obtain node names and separators")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Herve Codina <herve.codina@bootlin.com>
Reviewed-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Petr Mladek <pmladek@suse.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231114152655.409331-1-herve.codina@bootlin.com

diff --git a/lib/vsprintf.c b/lib/vsprintf.c
index 3e3733a7084f..552738f14275 100644
--- a/lib/vsprintf.c
+++ b/lib/vsprintf.c
@@ -2111,15 +2111,20 @@ char *fwnode_full_name_string(struct fwnode_handle *fwnode, char *buf,
 
 	/* Loop starting from the root node to the current node. */
 	for (depth = fwnode_count_parents(fwnode); depth >= 0; depth--) {
-		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode =
-			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth);
+		/*
+		 * Only get a reference for other nodes (i.e. parent nodes).
+		 * fwnode refcount may be 0 here.
+		 */
+		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode = depth ?
+			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth) : fwnode;
 
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name_prefix(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 
-		fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
+		if (depth)
+			fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
 	}
 
 	return buf;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `lib/vsprintf.c`**
- The loop that iterates over the current node and its parents has been modified to avoid obtaining a reference for the current node when its reference count may be zero.
- The condition for obtaining a reference to the fwnode has been changed: now, a reference is only obtained for parent nodes (when `depth` is greater than 0). The current node is directly used without obtaining a reference.
- The call to `fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode)` is now conditional; it is only called if `depth` is greater than 0, ensuring that the current node is not released when its reference count is already zero.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The changes made in `lib/vsprintf.c` are directly related to fixing a refcount issue that occurs when the current node is being destroyed. By modifying the way references are handled in the `fwnode_full_name_string` function, the patch prevents the situation where a reference is dropped on a node that is already being released, thus avoiding the warning and potential crash. This change ensures that the function can safely print the full name of a node even while it is in the process of being destroyed, thereby addressing the bug reported in the patch description.

Signed-off-by: Herve Codina <herve.codina@bootlin.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by a reference count issue in the `__fwnode_link_del()` function, where a `pr_debug()` call attempts to print the full name of an fwnode that is being destroyed. This results in a situation where the reference count of the fwnode reaches zero, leading to a warning and potential crash when the code tries to obtain or drop references to the current node during its destruction process.

Here is the patch:
 
 static noinline_for_stack
 char *fwnode_full_name_string(struct fwnode_handle *fwnode, char *buf,
 			      char *end)
 {
 	int depth;
 
 	/* Loop starting from the root node to the current node. */
 	for (depth = fwnode_count_parents(fwnode); depth >= 0; depth--) {
-		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode =
-			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth);
+		/*
+		 * Only get a reference for other nodes (i.e. parent nodes).
+		 * fwnode refcount may be 0 here.
+		 */
+		struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode = depth ?
+			fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth) : fwnode;
 
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name_prefix(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 		buf = string(buf, end, fwnode_get_name(__fwnode),
 			     default_str_spec);
 
-		fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
+		if (depth)
+			fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
 	}
 
 	return buf;
 }

```

```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `fwnode_get_nth_parent()` function is called to obtain a reference to the current node (or its parents) while the fwnode is being destroyed. This leads to a situation where the reference count can reach zero, causing a warning and potential crash when the code attempts to drop the reference with `fwnode_handle_put()`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
struct fwnode_handle *__fwnode = depth ?
    fwnode_get_nth_parent(fwnode, depth) : fwnode;
```
```c
if (depth)
    fwnode_handle_put(__fwnode);
```
Reason:
The fix modifies the logic to avoid obtaining a reference for the current node when it is being destroyed. By checking if `depth` is non-zero before calling `fwnode_get_nth_parent()`, the code ensures that no reference is taken for the current node, thus preventing the reference count issue and allowing the full name to be printed safely.
